desc:
The strings a and b each hold a non-negative integer written in decimal. Return their sum as a decimal string.

The numbers can have thousands of digits, so you must add them digit by digit, the way you do on paper, instead of converting the whole strings to integers.

Example: a = "456", b = "77" gives "533". Example: a = "999", b = "1" gives "1000".
constraints: a and b contain only the digits 0-9
Neither string has leading zeros, except for the string "0" itself
hints: Start at the last digit of each string and walk to the left, remembering a carry.
At each position the column total is digitA + digitB + carry. The digit you write is total % 10 and the new carry is total // 10. A string that has run out of digits contributes 0.
Keep going while either string still has digits or the carry is non-zero (so 999 + 1 grows a new leading digit). Collect digits in a list and reverse it once at the end.
editorial: Use two indices starting at the ends of the strings and a carry initialised to 0. Each step adds the current digit of each string (0 when a string is exhausted) plus the carry, appends total % 10 to an output list and sets carry = total // 10. The loop stops when both indices have left their strings and the carry is 0. The output list holds the digits from least to most significant, so it is reversed before joining.

The carry is never more than 1 because the largest possible column total is 9 + 9 + 1 = 19. Since neither input has leading zeros, the result has none either. Time is linear in the longer input; appending to a list and reversing once avoids the quadratic cost of prepending to a string.
solution:
def addDecimalStrings(a, b):
    i, j = len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1
    carry = 0
    out = []
    while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
        total = carry
        if i >= 0:
            total += ord(a[i]) - 48
            i -= 1
        if j >= 0:
            total += ord(b[j]) - 48
            j -= 1
        out.append(chr(48 + total % 10))
        carry = total // 10
    out.reverse()
    return "".join(out) if out else "0"
